scope: Monaco 0.57.0 internal Myers algorithm versus an original exact changed-span implementation; no whole editor or full internal result API parity claim.
methodology: Three fresh invocations of the existing comparator with its original case definitions and unmodified worker. Each invocation uses separate fresh processes per algorithm and case, 30 warmups and 200 timed calls, alternating algorithm order by case. Getter inputs are constructed before timing, and replay is checked after every timed call. The summary takes the median of the three per-case run medians; it is not a pooled-sample median or a confidence interval. Prior-run timings are historical context, while fresh original timings are the current comparison. Peak RSS is whole-process. Same host, no independent-host replication.

receipt.scope: Monaco 0.57.0 internal Myers algorithm versus an original exact changed-span implementation; no whole editor or full internal result API parity claim.
receipt.methodology: Same getter-based sequence input constructed before timing; both return changed spans and hitTimeout. Execution order alternates by case. p05/p95 are observed sample quantiles, not confidence intervals. Peak RSS covers the whole worker, imports, validation and inputs. Single-machine exploratory comparison with no independent replication or original deadline/result-helper comparison.

changes: Call bounded getter sequences directly, preserving the method receiver and avoiding an extra forwarding closure.
Store only reachable diagonal parity in 16-bit trace layers, and reuse each layer as its frontier instead of copying or filling a whole-input frontier.
Retain the original distance-999 search budget and linear-space fallback; coordinates fit within 10,999.
Reconstruct changed spans from equal runs rather than allocating and reversing one pair per matching element; linear-space reconstruction also emits spans directly.
Return a sole unequal pair immediately after common-boundary trimming, without frontier allocation or redundant getter reads.

cases: Independent exact-cost recurrence on 1,000 random inputs and all 961 binary sequence pairs through four lines.
Exact reconstruction at shortest-path distances 998 and 999, and the distance-1,000 fallback.
10,000-element getter sequences with six sparse changes, receiver preservation and checked getter index bounds.
800/780-element duplicate-heavy fallback compared with independent minimum-cost recurrence.
Existing large-distance sparse overlap, disjoint input, declared bounds and Editor file integration checks.
A single changed pair requires exactly the common-boundary getter reads, with no additional search reads.
